To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) subjects are able to discriminate between different levels of beat strength, and that (b) the discrimination between strong and intermediate beat levels depends on the metrical structure.
We show that attention is allocated to an intermediate metrical level in the presence of conflicting cues.

(1) subjects can be made to respond faster when they are cued to the onset of an intermediate beat strength in a 6/8 meter and (2) subjects respond faster to a cue that occurs at the onset of the strong beat of a 6/4 meter than they do to a cue that is presented at the weak beat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of attention in the perception of musical metrical structure.
the perception and cognition of rhythm, and in particular, the perception and cognition underlying the experience of metrical structure.
the role of attentional resources in the perception of musical metrical structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the human auditory system has an attentional mechanism which allows for the detection of the metrical structure of music, and that this attentional effect is sensitive to the relative beat strength of the musical metrical structure.
the results of this study indicate that attention can be directed to an intermediate level in the metrical hierarchy.

the results of the current experiment are in line with the theory of metrical structure, but do not provide evidence for a more detailed distinction between different levels of metrical strength than that between strong and weak beats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
metrical structure is a graded property, with a hierarchy of beat strengths, and that attention can be focused on intermediate beat strengths.
the human auditory system is sensitive to the hierarchical structure of metrical patterns, and that this sensitivity is not restricted to strong beats.
musical metrical structure can be used as a means of directing attention to intermediate levels of strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metrical structure has an impact on attention, even at an intermediate level of metrical strength.
metrical structure can be used as an additional dimension to modulate attention.
the human auditory system is sensitive to metrical structure at a more fine graded level than previously thought.
